title: Rails request: route, scope, params, response
outcome: Trace a Rails 4.2 action and protect record ownership at the server.
book: Metaprogramming Ruby part II: reading Rails declarations

exercises.title: Find and fix the bug
exercises.prompt: The update action uses Task.find(id), permits title, and checks only that a user is logged in. Repair the cross-user write.

exercises.title: Change one condition
exercises.prompt: A background job also updates tasks. Where should the reusable business rule live?

trace.title: Rack and route
trace.detail: Rails connects a Rack request to a route, a controller action, model work, and a response. A before_action can establish a current user. It does not automatically limit every database lookup to that user.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
Trace PUT /tasks/7: route chooses update; authentication runs; the scoped find either returns an allowed task or raises not found; permitted input reaches update; the action chooses JSON and status.

The private helper cannot be called as a public action. Use request tests for missing authentication, another user’s ID, rejected attributes, validation errors, and a successful update. Also assert the database row stayed unchanged on rejection.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: Task.find(params[:id]) plus permit(:title) still allows an ownership bug. Strong parameters protect allowed attributes, not which task you can edit. Never permit owner_id just because the browser sent it.
